newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Feb 3.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- Qin Jiwei, former defence minister and state councillor, dies in Beijing on February 2
- Some 900,000 students will graduate from various universities and colleges this year
- Liu Mingzhu elected to head Standing Committee of the People's Congress in Inner Mongolia.
- China and the United States reached a new textile trade agreement following six days of "tough but fruitful" negotiations.
- China's paper and paper board demand in 1997 is expected to reach 29 million tonnes
- China's demand for sedan cars is expected to reach 450,000 to 476,000 units in 1997
- China issues new principles for approving contruction materials projects invested in by foreign businesses.
- Finance Minister Liu Zhongli says China will maintain its tight fiscal policy in 1997
- The Bank of Communications posts 5.357 billion yuian in profits in 1996
- China plans to set up a nationwide unified tax collection and auditing system by the year 2010.

- While China's private sector is seen accounting for 20.2 percent of GNP by the year 2000, collective firms and the state sector are seen representing 41.3 and 35.8 percent respectively by the same year.
- Shanghai's textile industry registered profits of 10 million yuan at the end of 1996 after making losses of 350 million in the first seven months.
